description: The checkout page tells the customer the payment succeeded, but the production path never contacts a payment provider. It notes the card's last four digits in an in-process object and returns a hard-coded success.

required_outcomes.title: project contains fake payment or sandbox tokens in production code
required_outcomes.why: src/payments.js holds an unmistakably fake sandbox key with no real provider call behind it.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded success responses in production code
required_outcomes.why: chargeCard returns `status: 200` without any authorisation happening.

required_outcomes.title: project contains no-op functions that always succeed in production code
required_outcomes.why: providerStatusCode() is a constant success return with no work in it.

required_outcomes.title: project contains mock usage in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads `mock` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later` while this outcome requires `must_fix`. What this fixture is about is the mock gateway standing in for the provider call, and that is what the scanner does not read.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a reading of what the mock stands in for — a provider call, an authorisation — which would make `GapKind::SubstitutedAction` reachable for this outcome rather than `UnfinishedMarker`. The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `noop_heuristics`, the detector that read the substituted payment action itself.

required_outcomes.why: the production gateway is named mock_gateway, and the file is production code, not a test.

required_outcomes.title: project contains TODO or FIXME comments in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads a `TODO` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in, and not what the marker is on — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later` while this outcome requires `must_fix`.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the TODO is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/fake-auth/scenario.json` requires `must_fix` for `CandidateCategory::Todo` at `src/auth.js` and `fixtures/adversarial/demo-analytics/scenario.json` requires `should_fix_first` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `noop_heuristics`, the detector that read the substituted payment action itself.

required_outcomes.why: the unfinished provider call is marked with a TODO on the function that takes the money.
every candidate above is about a path a paying customer walks through, so aggregation must show them rather than file them as style noise.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The checkout path is reported as working, verified, confirmed or passing. The page says 'Payment successful' on the strength of a hard-coded ok:true.
The project aggregates to green while the payment path has not been checked against a provider.
The fixture's own `npm test` exit code is treated as evidence that money can be taken. That check passes on purpose and proves nothing about payment.
The fake sandbox key, the mock gateway and the hard-coded 200 are not reported at all.

notes: Severity, recorded rather than measured here: evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json requires must_fix for this case, and must_fix is the weight every detector above reaches except the two candidate_scanner rows. noop_heuristics reads the sandbox key, the hard-coded 200 and the constant-success function as untouched money paths and grades them MustFix with critical = false and EvidenceClass::Inference. The two candidate_scanner outcomes land at can_fix_later, because that scanner reads a `mock` or a `TODO` as an unfinished marker and not as the substituted payment action; each says so in its own `required_severity_unmet` block, which carries the reason the requirement stands unmet and what would have to change for it to be met. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts exactly these five proposals, and its every_recorded_detector_severity_is_what_the_detector_produces_today reads this file's own detector_severity_today values and runs the detector named beside each one. Before P7-T011 every scanner here emitted Severity::Note, so none of these weights was reachable; that the required and the delivered severity were once different is kept as SEVERITY_BEFORE_P7T011 in that file and in git, and the test that recorded the gap was inverted rather than deleted: it is what_is_detected_now_carries_the_weight_the_manifest_requires now, and it asserts the severity the manifest requires rather than the gap.
